name: Beth Peor
overview: Beth Peor is identified in Scripture as a location within the territory of the tribe of Reuben, situated near the land of Moab. It is described as being opposite a valley where the Israelites camped after defeating King Sihon of the Amorites, highlighting its geographical significance in the conquest narrative. Notably, Beth Peor is closely associated with the burial site of Moses, a sacred and mysterious place whose exact location remains unknown, underscoring God's sovereign preservation of His servant's resting place. This connection anchors Beth Peor as a meaningful landmark in Israel's journey and God's unfolding plan.
